evidence: DeepSeek checks `if p1 + p2 > T`; GPT checks `if sum_in > T` and then looks for causal violation; Qwen checks `p1_total > T` and `p2_total > T`; GLM checks `if p1 + p2 > T` and then prints `LOAD 2`.
affordance_in_statement: The router can schedule at most one Ingress packet per timeslot ... The router can schedule at most one Egress packet per timeslot ... For a schedule to be valid, the following verification routine must return `PASS` ... Exactly one of the following foundational requirements is broken.
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal: the existing firewall and two independent per-timeslot capacities mathematically reduce the task to p1_i + p2_i > T, sum(p1_i) > T, and sum(p2_i) > T. Defeating this approach requires changing the scheduling semantics, such as adding a non-count-based per-flow spacing or ordering constraint.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: At most one packet of each channel can be scheduled per timeslot, and the firewall forbids ingress after that flow's first egress.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Computes `p1_total` and `p2_total` and classifies saturation before checking causal feasibility.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each channel has an independent capacity of one packet per timeslot.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the per-flow `p1 + p2 > T` test, then relies on the exactly-one guarantee to output `LOAD 2` when the other tests fail.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Every provided configuration is guaranteed to break exactly one foundational requirement.

common_affordance: The firewall plus independent one-packet-per-channel capacities make feasibility completely characterizable by three scalar inequalities: p1_i + p2_i > T, sum(p1_i) > T, or sum(p2_i) > T.
recommended_edit: To defeat all survivors, change the mutable scheduling semantics by adding a genuine non-count-based per-flow constraint, such as requiring consecutive packets of the same flow to be separated by an intervening timeslot. This makes causal feasibility depend on packet placement rather than only on p1_i + p2_i, while preserving the input and output formats.
